title: Live runs of the judgment suite, behind a flag and caps that hold
request: Add a live evaluation of a configured model on the A4.1 cases. Show the estimated requests and the cap and ask for --yes; run each case several times (5 by default) because a model's answers vary; report each score as a mean with a 95% interval, plus tokens and cost from the gateway; store the result under evidence/campaigns with a run id and the model's name; say that scores are evidence about this model on these traps, not about production readiness.
spec: make agent-eval-live needs an explicit flag, prints requests, tokens and cost before it starts, refuses to exceed a stated cap, and reports scores with intervals over repeated runs. Done when a run on a local model prints per-case results and a table of scores with their spread, and no run starts without the flag.
plan: Write dclab_rnd/agent_eval/live.py: the intern, driven by the configured model through the workspace gateway, on the A4.1 cases (all or --cases), --repeats times; print the plan (model, runs, upper bounds) and send nothing without --yes.
Store results as AEV-NNN_judgment_v1_live_<model>.json, never overwritten; the Benchmark page reads only scripted results.
Run check-all and the review in parallel; fix the eight findings, rewriting the runner.
Meet the Done-when with a real, free run: point the intern's tiers at a local Ollama (qwen2.5-coder 1.5B) for this command only, 3 cases x 2 repeats, with a request cap.
Fix the re-check's remaining finding by keeping every request in the suite the intern's own; commit the draft pipeline race found by the gate separately.

decisions.decision: During the suite only the intern talks to the model; tools that would ask one of their own (leakage review, project answer, stage notes and explanations) take their deterministic paths.
decisions.why: Then the session's caps and accounting cover every request; the alternative, a per-run project cap in the gateway plus usage read back per project, was more machinery for the same guarantee.

decisions.decision: A run cut short by a cap or an error is recorded as not run, never scored, and the suite stops there.
decisions.why: Scoring a refused run as a miss reports a score no model produced.

decisions.decision: Intervals are taken over complete repeats only; per-case counts include every scored run.
decisions.why: Averaging repeats with different case sets mixes different questions into one rate.

decisions.decision: Refuse a euro cap on an unpriced model, and refuse a priced remote intern model without one.
decisions.why: A euro cap on an unpriced model can never stop anything, so printing it as a cap would be false comfort.

change: dclab_rnd/agent_eval/live.py and make agent-eval-live: a printed plan with upper bounds on requests (runs x (tool calls + 2)), input tokens (each request carries the policy, the schemas and up to all earlier results) and euros when priced; --yes, --cases, --repeats (5 by default, at most 10), --max-requests counted at the transport, --cap-eur split over runs as each session's cap; results with a run id, the model and prompt hashes; tests/test_agent_eval_live.py.

findings.defect: Engine and tool requests bypassed every cap, the bound and the reported spend.
findings.scenario: With --max-requests 3 and a scripted model that calls review_leakage twice, 3 requests were counted and 2 leakage-review requests were sent uncounted, missing from the tokens; run_all makes two stage_notes requests per stage (10 per run) on the standard tier, which can be a priced remote model while the intern's strong tier is local.
findings.cause: Only the intern's own client was wrapped by the counter; tools built their own clients from installed().
findings.fix: Counting moved to the transport of the installed gateway; stage notes, explanations and project answers are switched off during the suite.
findings.test: A test that a tool's model request is counted.
findings.impact: With the intern on a local model and the standard tier on a priced remote one, a live run could send ten paid stage-note requests per run_all outside every cap and outside the reported spend, so --cap-eur would not bound the bill.

findings.defect: Refused and failed runs were stored as real scores.
findings.scenario: A priced scripted model, --cap-eur 4, 3 cases x 4 repeats: all 12 runs were refused with 0 requests sent, and the file said status completed, 'Requests 12', leaks caught 0.0 [0.0, 0.0].
findings.cause: The counter incremented before the gateway's check; a session ended by a refusal or an error was scored; 'stopped' was set only when spend reached the cap exactly.
findings.fix: Count after the gateway accepts a request; a failed or budget-stopped session is not run and stops the suite; refuse to start when one request's estimate exceeds --cap-eur.
findings.test: A test where every request is refused: the first run is not scored, status stopped, 0 requests.
findings.impact: A suite whose every request was refused was stored as a completed run scoring 0 leaks caught: an evidence file reporting a model failure that never happened, ready to become a baseline.

findings.defect: A run cut by the cap was scored, and a partial repeat entered the interval.
findings.scenario: --max-requests 10, 3 cases x 2 repeats: every completed run caught the leak, yet leaks caught came out 0.5 [0.0, 1.0], n=2.
findings.cause: The interrupted run counted as a miss, and repeats with different case sets were averaged.
findings.fix: The interrupted run is not scored; intervals use complete repeats only (here 1.0, n=1).
findings.test: A request-cap test with a partial repeat.
findings.impact: A run where every completed case caught the leak reported 0.5 [0.0, 1.0], halving the model's score because the cap cut a run.

findings.defect: The command-line gateway had no usage log.
findings.scenario: installed() returned a gateway with no usage, so nothing reached the workspace usage log and the workspace monthly cap was skipped.
findings.cause: The command did not install the workspace gateway, unlike every other command-line tool.
findings.fix: for_workspace() is the default gateway and is installed for the run.
findings.impact: Benchmark spending never reached the workspace usage log or its monthly cap, so the Admin page and the monthly limit could not see it.

findings.defect: --max-requests 0 gave the full upper bound, and --max-steps was not checked against the session's limits.
findings.scenario: --yes --max-requests 0 ran with a cap of runs x 18 instead of sending nothing; --max-steps 1 printed a bound of runs x 3 while each session allows at least 3 tool calls.
findings.fix: --max-requests must be at least 1; --max-steps must be between 3 and 80.
findings.impact: --max-requests 0, the natural way to say 'send nothing', would send up to the full bound.

findings.defect: The printed 'at most' euros was not an upper bound.
findings.scenario: It assumed 40,000 characters per request; the tool schemas are about 10,800 characters, the policy about 1,600, and each tool result adds up to 6,000, so by the 16th request a prompt is about 108,000 characters: roughly 1.6 times the printed figure.
findings.cause: A flat per-request estimate for a conversation that grows.
findings.fix: The bound grows with each request's conversation, a token bound is printed, and a euro cap on an unpriced model is refused.
findings.test: A plan test on the printed bounds.
findings.impact: The owner approves a run with --yes after reading an 'at most' euro figure that real runs could exceed by about 1.6 times, before counting side requests.
alternatives: Print the figure as an estimate instead of a bound, the reviewer's other option: set aside because the plan is what the owner approves before --yes; it now grows with each request's conversation and a token bound is printed.

findings.defect: The status row described guarantees the code did not keep, and marked the package done while its Done-when was not met.
findings.scenario: The row said --max-requests counts every request and that nothing goes to a priced remote model without --cap-eur; no local-model run existed.
findings.cause: The row was written before the run and before the review.
findings.fix: The row was rewritten after the fixes, and AEV-002 was run on a local model and stored.
findings.impact: The status row would tell the next session that the caps cover every request and that the package is done, so later work would build on guarantees that did not exist.

findings.defect: The euro cap and the reported tokens and euros still left out the leakage-review requests (re-check).
findings.scenario: Every tier a priced scripted model with large usage, the model calling review_leakage four times per run, 2 cases x 2 repeats, --cap-eur 40: the suite completed with 36 requests (16 by the leakage review) and reported 2.4 euros, while the usage log showed 818.4 euros.
findings.cause: The run's euro limit was set only on the intern's client, and the run's spend was read from the session, which counts only the intern.
findings.fix: During the suite only the intern talks to the model; the leakage review takes its deterministic path.
findings.test: A test like the reviewer's: no leakage-review request is sent during the suite.
findings.impact: In the reviewer's run the suite reported 2.4 euros while the usage log showed 818.4: a priced standard tier could spend hundreds of times the cap the owner set.
alternatives: Give the gateway a per-run project cap and read each run's euros and tokens back from the usage log by project: set aside as more machinery for the same guarantee; the leakage review takes its deterministic path during the suite instead.
findings.open: The printed request bound covers the intern only; the reviewer judged this safe, since other requests would stop the suite early rather than overspend.

findings.defect: The PostgreSQL run of the draft flow test failed once on a draft whose data was 'ready' but had no analysis.
findings.scenario: A reader between two writes (the page, the Home agent, or a test polling for 'ready') saw a ready asset with no analysis.
findings.cause: The pipeline saved the asset as ready in one update and the analysis, cleaning log and active asset in the next.
findings.fix: Both go in one update (separate commit).
findings.test: The draft flow tests on PostgreSQL.
findings.impact: The page, the Home agent or a test could read a draft marked ready with no analysis and act on it; in the gate it failed once on PostgreSQL.

measurements.name: AEV-002, first live run (local qwen2.5-coder 1.5B through Ollama, 3 cases x 2 repeats)
measurements.gate: A run on a local model prints per-case results and a table of scores with their spread (the package's Done-when); scores are evidence about this model on these traps only.
measurements.result: Per-case lines and the interval table were printed and stored. The model answered each case in one reply without calling a tool, so it kept 0 of 2 leaks out per repeat (0.0, interval 0.0 to 0.0, n=2) and made no move; 6 requests, about 16,000 input and 3,500 output tokens, 0 euros.
measurements.next: The harness gate passes; the model fails the traps. Run a larger local or remote model with a euro cap; the token bound is generous; a live run does not set the Benchmark leaderboard yet.
measurements.against_gate: The gate asks for per-case results and a table of scores with their spread from a run on a local model: both were printed and stored, so the harness passes. The model's own score, 0 of 2 leaks kept out per repeat (0.0, interval 0.0 to 0.0, n=2), is not what the gate judges.
limits: 3 cases x 2 repeats is a smoke run: it shows the harness works on a real model, not how any model scores on the suite.
The model answered without calling a tool, so the traps were never reached; the result says this model did not use the tools, nothing about judgment.
An interval of 0.0 to 0.0 over n=2 is two identical outcomes, not a precise estimate.
Nothing was priced (0 euros), so the euro cap was not exercised by a real run.

outcome: Done: make agent-eval-live prints its plan, needs --yes, holds its request and euro caps over every request of the suite, never scores a cut run, and stores AEV results with intervals over complete repeats. Eight findings and one re-check finding fixed; a draft race found by the gate fixed separately.
lessons: A cap that wraps one client is not a cap when tools build their own clients; count at the transport or keep the other callers off the model.
A run refused by a budget must be 'not run', never a scored miss: otherwise the cap writes the result.
An upper bound for a growing conversation must grow with it.
The Done-when of a measurement package is met only by a real run, here a free local one.
risks: A cap that wraps only the intern's client while tools build their own clients and spend outside it.
Runs refused by a budget, or failed by a model server that is down, being scored as misses.
An 'at most' cost printed from a flat estimate for a conversation that grows with every request.
Averaging repeats that covered different cases into one interval.
Live traffic missing the workspace usage log and its monthly cap.
